title: Unit tests for BookingService
idea: A test case calls one public method with known inputs and checks the result, so you can prove the booking rules still hold after every change.
points: Each test follows arrange, act, assert: set up, call once, check the outcome.
Inject an in-memory `BookingRepository` so tests need no database.
Test the boundaries: back-to-back slots, exact overlaps and empty slots.
Assert on public results and error codes, never on private fields.

messages.label: new BookingService(repo)
messages.note: Arrange: the test builds the service with a fake repository it controls.

messages.label: book('e1', 'R1', 9, 10)
messages.note: Act: the test makes exactly one call through the public method.

messages.label: forRoom('R1')
messages.note: The service asks for existing bookings of that room, as it would in production.
The fake returns an empty list, so there is nothing to clash with.

messages.label: save(booking)
messages.note: No clash, so the service stores the new booking.

messages.label: booking
messages.note: Assert: the test compares the returned booking with the one it expects.

code.title: Four focused tests
code.caption: A tiny `check` helper keeps the output stable. Add a test that the same slot in room `R2` is allowed.

walk.text: The fake has only the two methods `book` needs, `save` and `forRoom`, named as in the real one.
Each error is a c05-t05 class carrying a stable `code`, so tests never match message text.
`check` runs one test and prints `ok` or `FAIL` with the reason.
Every test gets a fresh service, so no state leaks between tests.
Arrange, act and assert, one line each, for the happy path.
Back-to-back slots share an edge; the strict `<` check must allow them.
An empty slot is invalid input, caught before any lookup.

pitfalls: Do not share one service across tests; earlier bookings will break later tests.
Test the edge where one slot ends as the next begins.
Avoid asserting on log lines or private state; they change during refactors.

quiz.q: Which test would catch both `<` in the overlap check becoming `<=`?
options: Booking a free room returns a booking
Booking 10–11 after 9–10 in the same room succeeds
Booking 9–10 twice in the same room fails
quiz.why: With `<=`, a slot ending at 10 and one starting at 10 count as clashing. Only the back-to-back test notices.

takeaway: Test through the public method, with fakes, at the boundaries.
